00:36 XERJ is a free, self-hosted alternative to Elasticsearch. xerj — XERJ is the new way for AI to search data. Its autoindex capability activates agents to know your data without the token waste of grep and sed. One command indexes code, docs, logs and PDFs for search, RAG, security audits and agent memory, using 40x fewer tokens than grep. Elasticsearch compatible, so existing clients just work. 01:30 Same AI agent. 5 different frameworks. The gap shocked me. 🤯 I rebuilt the same order-return agent in OpenAI Agents SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, PydanticAI, LangGraph and Google ADK - same virtual machine, no database, simulated AI model, then pushed traffic until each one broke. The best handled 270 active users at once. The worst only 80. Same agent, same machine. A 3.4x gap. The framework you pick is not a small detail. It decides how far your agent can scale. Someone built an open-source inference engine that can run massive AI models on a single mini PC! Meet Kyojin, an open-source project by Yamz Labs designed to run large language models locally on AMD Strix Halo hardware. What's impressive is that it can run 300B-class Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on a mini PC equipped with 128GB of unified memory. No massive GPU server required. Meet KittenTTS, an open-source text-to-speech project designed to generate natural-sounding speech while supporting CPU-based inference. What's interesting about this project is that you don't necessarily need an expensive GPU to run it locally.
